summary: The paper proposes Neighbor Distance Minimization (NDM), an unsupervised method that learns an orthogonal rotation of representation space so that a partition into orthogonal subspaces minimizes the intra-subspace nearest-neighbor distance, motivated by a feature-group / mutual-exclusiveness view of superposition and equivalently as total-correlation minimization. Evaluation spans a toy model (where ground truth is recovered), GPT-2 Small (a 5-test quantitative suite using known IOI/Greater-than circuits with a Gini-inequality metric, where NDM beats Identity/Random/PCA/SAE-clustering baselines on average), qualitative preimage analysis, and a suggestive scaling test on Qwen2.5-1.5B and Gemma-2-2B for context/parametric knowledge routing. The direction and evidence are genuinely useful for interpretability, but the empirical package has soft spots (unconventional Gini metric with a self-defined 0.6 threshold, no error bars/seeds, uneven per-test wins, 2B evidence is largely illustrative), and positioning against unsupervised representation decomposition literature (ICA, disentanglement, rotation-based interpretability) is thin.
strengths: Novel unsupervised angle on subspace discovery: prior subspace work (DAS and follow-ups) requires a human-specified causal abstraction, while NDM only needs activations, which is a meaningful methodological contribution.
The MI/total-correlation reinterpretation makes the objective principled beyond the feature-group toy story and gracefully handles cases where strict mutual exclusiveness does not hold.
Multi-scale evaluation: toy model with ground-truth W recovery, GPT-2 Small with known circuits and 5 targeted tests, and a scaling probe on two ~2B LMs including knowledge-routing counterfactuals.

Baselines are reasonable and non-trivial for an unsupervised method (Identity, Random, two PCA orderings, SAE-feature clustering adapted from Engels et al.); NDM wins on average across three normalization variants.
Sensible mechanism for choosing subspace dimensionality via MI-thresholded merging, with acknowledgement that this is heuristic and alternatives were tried (App. G.4).
Limitations section is honest about non-fine-grained partitions, reliance on Linear Representation Hypothesis, and cases where small subspaces resist interpretation.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical soundness of the headline claim is weak: Table 1 reports single-point Gini numbers with no seeds, no confidence intervals, and no significance tests, even though NDM is a stochastic optimization over an orthogonal matrix and the merging procedure is threshold-dependent. Several per-test cells show NDM losing to baselines (e.g., test 3 dS = 0.63 vs Feature 0.73; test 4 dS = 0.38), so the 'clear outperformance' rests on averages without variance.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over multiple seeds for NDM (and, where stochastic, baselines) for every cell of Table 1; state a paired significance test on the per-test wins; add a sensitivity curve over the MI merge threshold.

key_concerns.issue: The evaluation metric is self-defined and self-thresholded: the paper uses Gini over subspace patching effects and declares 'satisfactory' at >0.6 based on its own App. D.4 examples. This weakens external comparability, especially given that concentration depends on the (also self-chosen) dimension configuration output by NDM, which baselines are then forced to inherit. This risks a mild metric/baseline framing bias.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report at least one standard, off-the-shelf localization metric alongside Gini (e.g., fraction of patching effect captured by top-k subspaces at matched total dimension, or an IIA-style score); redo Table 1 with each baseline using its own preferred dimension split and take a Pareto view.

key_concerns.issue: The 2B scaling story is largely illustrative rather than quantitative. Figure 5 highlights one 'parametric' and one 'context' subspace in specific layers, but there is no aggregate metric across layers/models/prompts, no baseline comparison in the main text (baselines are deferred to Fig. 19/20 in appendix), and no null test for how often a random rotation would produce a similarly asymmetric subspace by chance under this counterfactual setup.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a summary quantitative measure of asymmetry (parametric vs. context patching effect) across all layers and all seeds, with baselines, and a permutation/random-rotation null.

key_concerns.issue: Related work under-engages the most directly comparable non-interpretability literature. Unsupervised decomposition of representation space by learning an orthogonal rotation is closely related to ICA, disentanglement (β-VAE / factor-VAE), and prior 'rotate-then-partition' probing work; none of these are discussed or compared. Within interpretability, no direct comparison to raw SAE features (only a clustering of SAE features) is provided.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a subsection distinguishing NDM from ICA/whitening and disentanglement methods (which also target statistical independence between components), and include at least one classical ICA-style baseline in Table 1; briefly justify why clustered SAEs (not raw SAEs) are the right feature-based comparator.

key_concerns.issue: The feature-group / mutual-exclusiveness motivation is only verified in a very small toy model (z=40, d=12, two groups of 20). App. C.1 is invoked but not shown in-body. It is unclear how robust the recovery is as group counts, group sizes, and co-activation regimes vary, and whether NDM degrades gracefully when feature groups partially overlap.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Bring one or two of the App. C.1 configurations into the main text and add a systematic sweep (varying #groups, group size, activation sparsity, and controlled cross-group correlation) with a recovery-quality metric.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility is uneven: the algorithm and toy setting are clear, but MI-threshold values, dimension configurations found for each model/layer, KSG estimator settings, number of activations used per layer, and orthogonal-matrix parametrization/optimizer details are relegated to appendices whose density is not visible in-body. This is fine for a conference paper but the main text should still summarize the exact hyperparameters used to produce Table 1's 'best' row.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact hyperparameter table in the main Experiments section listing, per test, the MI threshold, initial dim config, merge schedule, and total training steps used for the reported NDM row.

key_concerns.issue: The qualitative preimage analysis relies on the authors' own prior tool ('InversionView', [Author] et al., 2024b) and on cosine similarity above 0.85 to define preimages. Since this is the sole evidence for the 'subspaces = variables' interpretability claim, sensitivity to the threshold and to the preimage database (2000 MiniPile + 2000 IOI/GT sequences) should be checked; otherwise the interpretability claim is threshold-dependent.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Show how preimage 'consistency' of a subspace varies with the cosine threshold and with an OOD probe set; report a quantitative interpretability score (e.g., an LLM- or human-judged consistency rate) rather than only illustrative figures.

key_concerns.issue: Some framing overshoots the evidence: the paper suggests NDM enables 'input-independent subspace circuits' as a downstream program, but no circuit is actually built in this paper — only concentration and knowledge-routing localization are demonstrated.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Reword the introduction and 'Future Directions' passages to scope the current contribution to subspace discovery + localization, and reserve subspace-circuit construction as future work.

questions_for_authors: How stable are the NDM partitions across seeds — do you recover subspaces with the same interpretations (current token, position, topic, etc.) each time, or only qualitatively similar ones? What is the seed-to-seed agreement (e.g., subspace-matching accuracy) for the reported GPT-2 layers?
What is the sensitivity of Table 1 to the MI merge threshold and to the initial (equal-sized) subspace configuration? Do the same qualitative conclusions hold across a reasonable range?

For each baseline in Table 1, how were the Gini numbers computed given that the dimension configuration was fixed to NDM's output — did you also try each baseline with its 'natural' or optimal dimension configuration, and does NDM still win?

How does raw SAE feature-level patching (rather than clusters of SAE features) compare on the same 5-test suite? And how does NDM compare against a classical ICA / whitening-plus-orthogonal-rotation baseline that also seeks statistically independent components?

In the 2B knowledge-conflict experiment, what fraction of subspaces (across all layers) exhibit strong parametric-only or context-only patching effects, relative to a random-rotation null? Is the effect shown in Fig. 5 typical or hand-picked?
How was the 0.6 Gini 'satisfactory' threshold established beyond the App. D.4 illustrations — is there a calibration against ground-truth localizations of known circuit variables?

You note (App. G.2) potential concerns from Makelov et al. about subspace interchange interventions creating illusory results; can you quantitatively rule out the illusion for the specific NDM subspaces reported (e.g., via a control task where the target variable is known to be absent)?

The intra-group superposition story requires (approximate) mutual exclusiveness within groups. Have you tested cases where features within a putative group are partially correlated rather than strictly mutually exclusive — does NDM still recover a clean partition or does it split them?
calibration_check: Claims about GPT-2 localization and unsupervised recovery in a toy model are appropriately scoped, but the 2B scaling framing and the pitched 'input-independent subspace circuits' program are stronger than what the current experiments demonstrate.

significance.justification: An unsupervised route to non-basis-aligned interpretable subspaces is a meaningful complement to DAS-style supervised subspace work and SAEs, and the interpretability community is likely to build on it.

novelty.justification: The specific neighbor-distance objective, together with its total-correlation reinterpretation and MI-based merging for dimension selection, is genuinely new relative to DAS, SAEs, and clustered-feature approaches, though it has clear conceptual cousins in ICA/disentanglement that go undiscussed.

rigor.justification: The method is well-motivated and the toy validation is clean, but the real-model evaluation depends heavily on a self-defined Gini metric with a self-set threshold, and dimension configurations are handed to baselines rather than optimized for them.

statistical_soundness.justification: No seeds, error bars, or significance tests accompany Table 1; NDM loses to at least one baseline on several individual cells, so the average-based headline is under-supported statistically.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper openly states that partitions are not fine-grained, that some small subspaces resist interpretation, and that 2B results must be read cautiously; a few forward-looking claims about subspace circuits do overshoot.

clarity.justification: The intuition, toy model, and GPT-2 evaluation are readable and well-organized, but the method section leans on appendices for hyperparameters and the merging procedure, and the equations for R and dist(·) are terse.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (Intro, Motivation, Method, Toy, LM experiments, Discussion, Limitations, Conclusion) with appropriate use of an appendix; length looks reasonable for ICLR.

reproducibility.justification: Algorithm 1, toy setup, MI/KSG estimator, and evaluation suite are described well enough in principle, but critical per-experiment hyperparameters (thresholds, initial configs, activation counts, optimizer) are pushed into appendices without a compact in-body summary.

related_work.justification: Interpretability positioning (DAS, SAEs, components, subspaces) is broadly correct, but the paper omits ICA, disentanglement, and other unsupervised rotation/decomposition literature that shares its objective in spirit.

figure_quality.justification: From captions, the figures directly support the claims — WᵀW block structure, RW recovery, preimage panels for the same token across subspaces, and knowledge-routing subspace effects — though the localization evidence (Fig. 5) is caption-illustrative rather than aggregated.

breadth_generality.justification: Toy + GPT-2 Small + two ~2B models cover a reasonable range, but the 2B evidence is qualitative-in-spirit and only one task family (knowledge routing) is probed at scale, limiting the generality actually demonstrated.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: an original unsupervised interpretability method with real evidence on GPT-2 and promising scaling signals, held back by soft statistical reporting, a self-defined evaluation metric, and thin positioning against unsupervised decomposition literature.
